findings.title: Missing license file
findings.explanation: No license file (such as LICENSE, LICENSE.txt, or COPYING) is present in the repository or referenced in metadata, meaning clear distribution permission is missing.
findings.suggestion: Add an open source license file (e.g., MIT, Apache-2.0, or BSD) to the repository.

items.title: No license file, headers or terms anywhere in the repository

findings.title: No license file, headers or terms anywhere in the repository
findings.evidence:
# Fiducials to model distance

This is an extension for 3D Slicer that computes distance between two point sets or a point set and a surface mesh.
findings.explanation: A repository-wide search for 'licen[cs]e|copyright|BSD|Apache|MIT' returned no matches: there is no LICENSE/COPYING file, no license header in FiducialsToModelDistance/FiducialsToModelDistance.py, and README.md states no terms. Without explicit permission, the Extensions Index cannot redistribute the extension in the binary package, so the 'clear distribution permission' admission requirement is unmet.
findings.suggestion: Add a LICENSE file (any OSI-approved license is acceptable, e.g. the Slicer BSD-3-Clause style) and reference it from README.md and the module's acknowledgementText.

findings.title: No license file or license terms in the repository
findings.evidence: This is an extension for 3D Slicer that computes distance between two point sets or a point set and a surface mesh.
findings.explanation: The repository has no LICENSE/COPYING file, and a text search for 'license' or 'copyright' across the repository returns nothing. README.md and the module header give no terms, so the extension and its contributors' code have no stated distribution permission. The index policy requires clear distribution terms before the extension can be offered to users.
findings.suggestion: Add a LICENSE file (any OSI-approved or equivalent license) at the repository root and state the license in README.md.

items.title: Hausdorff distance is computed with min() instead of max()

findings.title: Hausdorff distance is computed with min() instead of max()
findings.evidence:
# Hausdorff Distance is the max of the minimum distances
          inversePointDistances, inverseLabels = self.pointDistancesLabelsFromPoints(inputReference, inputPoints)
          metricLabels.append("Hausdorff Distance")
          metricValues.append(max(abs(pointDistances).min(), abs(inversePointDistances).min()))
findings.explanation: The symmetric Hausdorff distance is the maximum over both directions of the per-point minimum distances, but the code takes the minimum of the two minima. For the module's own test data (moving points 1.25-2.3 mm from the fixed set) the reported value is 1.25 mm instead of 2.3 mm, and the test at line 362 asserts the wrong value, so the bug is locked in. Users comparing registration accuracy would systematically under-report the worst-case error.
findings.suggestion: Use max(abs(pointDistances).max(), abs(inversePointDistances).max()) and update the expected value in the test to 2.3.

findings.title: Hausdorff metric is not the standard definition
findings.evidence:
# Hausdorff Distance is the max of the minimum distances
 metricValues.append(max(abs(pointDistances).min(), abs(inversePointDistances).min()))
findings.explanation: For fiducial-to-fiducial comparisons, the code takes max(min distance of A to B, min distance of B to A) (line 270). The symmetric Hausdorff distance is the max over points of the nearest-neighbour distance, so this min-based value can understate it. Users reporting it as Hausdorff could be misled.
findings.suggestion: Use the max of per-point nearest distances in each direction, or rename the metric and document the definition.

items.title: Catalog tracks moving branch 'master' instead of a pinned commit

findings.title: Catalog tracks moving branch 'master' instead of a pinned commit
findings.explanation: scm_revision is 'master', so the built extension is whatever master points to at build time. The reviewed commit 9ba774a39460fac85da215c5cfbbb19881094d6b is not what the index will build, and later changes would bypass review.
findings.suggestion: Pin scm_revision to a reviewed commit hash (or a release tag) in the catalog entry.

items.title: Long computation runs on the GUI thread without progress or cancellation

findings.title: Long computation runs on the GUI thread without progress or cancellation
findings.explanation: compute() is called directly from the button slot; the nested loops in pointDistancesLabelsFromPoints (lines 177-191) are O(n*m) and the surface path builds a vtkImplicitPolyDataDistance over the full mesh. With large fiducial sets or dense models Slicer freezes with no progress bar and no way to cancel, which looks like a crash to the user.
findings.suggestion: Use slicer.util.ProgressDialog / a CLI-style progress callback, or run the computation in a worker thread with progress and cancellation.

items.title: Metrics table is not cleared, so stale columns persist between runs

findings.title: Metrics table is not cleared, so stale columns persist between runs
findings.evidence:
if outputMetricsTable:
        import numpy as np
        metricValues = []
        metricLabels = []
findings.explanation: The distances table is cleared with RemoveAllColumns() (line 247) but the metrics table is only passed to slicer.util.updateTableFromArray, which adds/overwrites the named columns without removing others. If a user first computes fiducial-to-model metrics (Mean Absolute Distance, Maximum Absolute Distance, ...) and then fiducial-to-fiducial metrics into the same table, the absolute-distance columns remain and the table mixes results from two different runs.
findings.suggestion: Call outputMetricsTable.RemoveAllColumns() (or reset the table) before writing the new metrics.

items.title: Missing input validation for the input points node

findings.title: Missing input validation for the input points node
findings.evidence:
def compute(self, inputPoints, inputReference, outputMetricsTable, outputDistancesTable):

      if inputReference.IsA("vtkMRMLMarkupsFiducialNode"):
findings.explanation: compute() dereferences inputReference and inputPoints without None checks; the GUI selectors have noneEnabled=false so the normal path is safe, but the logic class is public API and the test calls it directly. A None input produces an AttributeError that is only caught by the generic handler in onApplyButton, giving a confusing message.
findings.suggestion: Validate that inputPoints and inputReference are not None and raise a clear ValueError.

items.title: No usage documentation, sample data or clinical disclaimer

findings.title: No usage documentation, sample data or clinical disclaimer
findings.evidence: This module was primarily designed to compute distances from a low density point cloud of fiducial points to the surface of a model.
findings.explanation: README.md only describes the purpose and shows two screenshots; there is no step-by-step tutorial, no sample scene, and no statement about intended (research) use. Users must guess the workflow, and there is no warning that the metrics are not validated for clinical decision making.
findings.suggestion: Add a short usage section (select input points, reference, output tables, press Apply) and a research-use disclaimer.

items.title: Signed minimum distance reported without documentation

findings.title: Signed minimum distance reported without documentation
findings.explanation: 'Minimum Distance' is computed from signed values (line 264) while 'Maximum Absolute Distance' is used for the surface case, so users get a negative minimum that is not explained in the UI or README. This is confusing for clinical error reporting.
findings.suggestion: Document the sign convention in the help text, or report absolute values consistently.

items.title: Surface distance uses the raw polydata without checking for a non-closed mesh

findings.title: Surface distance uses the raw polydata without checking for a non-closed mesh
findings.evidence:
# Transform model polydata to world coordinate system
      if inputModel.GetParentTransformNode():
findings.explanation: vtkImplicitPolyDataDistance returns signed distances whose sign depends on surface orientation, so for open or inconsistently oriented meshes the 'Mean Distance'/'Minimum Distance' values can be misleading while the absolute variants are fine. This is a documented-behaviour caveat rather than a crash, but the module presents signed values without any note.
findings.suggestion: Document that signed distances depend on mesh orientation and that absolute metrics should be used for open surfaces.

items.title: Test coverage and disclaimer are limited

findings.title: Test registration is partly commented out
findings.explanation: The Testing/Python directory contains only a commented-out registration, but the module's own unittest is still registered by slicer_add_python_unittest in FiducialsToModelDistance/CMakeLists.txt line 27, so the test does run. The empty directory is harmless clutter.
findings.suggestion: Remove the unused Testing/Python directory or add a real test file.

findings.title: Test coverage and disclaimer are limited
findings.explanation: The only test is a single ScriptedLoadableModuleTest case. The separate Testing/Python test file is commented out, and the test depends on a node named 'Model' existing (line 310). The README has no clinical-use disclaimer for a tool that computes surgical or registration error metrics.
findings.suggestion: Enable or remove the commented test, add a clinical-use disclaimer, and document sign and definition conventions for the metrics.

items.title: Catalog entry pins a moving branch and the source revision could not be verified

findings.title: Catalog entry pins a moving branch and the source revision could not be verified
findings.evidence: set(EXTENSION_DEPENDS "NA") # Specified as a space separated string, a list or 'NA' if any
findings.explanation: The catalog entry uses scm_revision 'master' and EXTENSION_DEPENDS 'NA' with empty build_dependencies, which is consistent with the source (no dependencies are used). I could not resolve the commit 9ba774a39460fac85da215c5cfbbb19881094d6b or the branch tip from this environment, so the exact reviewed revision is unverified; the code shown is what was reviewed.
findings.suggestion: No action required for the dependency settings; consider whether a fixed revision is preferable for reproducibility.
